title: Roman inscription at Laugaricio
description: Soldiers of the Second Legion wintering during the Marcomannic Wars carve an inscription into the castle rock, the northernmost trace of the Roman army in central Europe.

title: Church consecrated at Nitra
description: The archbishop of Salzburg consecrates a church for Prince Pribina, the first known Christian church among the western and eastern Slavs.

title: Battle of Pressburg
description: The Magyars destroy a Bavarian army, securing their hold on the Carpathian Basin, and the territory of Slovakia goes on to be part of Hungary for a thousand years.

title: Kremnica mint founded
description: King Charles I gives the mining town its privileges and a mint, which strikes the gold ducats of Hungary and is still at work.

title: Universitas Istropolitana founded
description: Pope Paul II approves the request of Matthias Corvinus for a university at Pressburg, the first on the territory of Slovakia.

title: Pressburg becomes the capital of Hungary
description: With central Hungary under Ottoman control, the diet makes Pressburg the seat of the kingdom's government, which it remains until 1783.

title: First coronation in St Martin's Cathedral
description: Maximilian II is crowned king of Hungary in Pressburg, the first of the coronations held there until 1830.

title: Synod of Žilina
description: Lutherans of Upper Hungary set up their own church organisation with three superintendents, independent of the Catholic bishops.

title: University of Trnava founded
description: Cardinal Péter Pázmány founds a Jesuit university, the main centre of learning in the kingdom until it moves to Buda in 1777.

title: Ottomans take Nové Zámky
description: The fortress of Nové Zámky surrenders to the grand vizier Köprülü Fazıl Ahmed and becomes the centre of an Ottoman province until 1685.

title: Prešov executions
description: A tribunal under General Antonio Caraffa tortures and executes 24 Protestant townsmen and nobles accused of supporting the Thököly uprising.

title: Maria Theresa crowned
description: Maria Theresa is crowned ruler of Hungary in Pressburg and wins the support of the Hungarian nobles in the War of the Austrian Succession.

title: Mining Academy founded
description: Maria Theresa founds a mining academy in the silver town of Banská Štiavnica, often counted as the first technical university in the world.

title: Peace of Pressburg
description: After its defeat at Austerlitz, Austria signs a peace with Napoleon in which it gives up Venetia, Tyrol and other lands.

title: Štúr's circle agrees a Slovak literary language
description: Ľudovít Štúr, Jozef Miloslav Hurban and Michal Miloslav Hodža meet at the parsonage of Hlboké and agree to base written Slovak on the central dialects, the basis of the modern standard.

title: Demands of the Slovak Nation
description: Slovak leaders adopt a programme asking for recognition as a nation, their own assembly and the use of Slovak in schools and offices.

title: Memorandum of the Slovak Nation
description: A national assembly in Martin asks the Hungarian parliament for a self-governing Slovak district and language rights.

title: Matica slovenská founded
description: Slovaks found a national cultural and scholarly society, which the Hungarian government closes in 1875.

title: Černová massacre
description: Gendarmes shoot fifteen villagers protesting at the consecration of their church without the priest Andrej Hlinka, drawing foreign attention to Hungary's treatment of its minorities.

title: Martin Declaration
description: The Slovak National Council declares that Slovaks will leave Hungary and join the Czechs in a common state.

title: Slovak Soviet Republic
description: A soviet republic is proclaimed in Prešov under the protection of the Hungarian Red Army and lasts about three weeks.

title: Žilina Agreement
description: A week after Munich, Slovak parties led by Hlinka's People's Party declare autonomy for Slovakia within Czechoslovakia, and Jozef Tiso forms a government.

title: Slovak State declared
description: Under pressure from Hitler the Slovak assembly declares independence, creating a state dependent on Germany the day before German troops enter Prague.

title: First transport of Jews leaves Poprad
description: About a thousand young women are sent to Auschwitz, the first of the transports by which the Slovak government deports some 58,000 Jews in 1942.

title: Slovak National Uprising
description: Part of the Slovak army and partisans rise against the incoming German forces and the Tiso government, holding central Slovakia for two months.

title: Košice Government Programme
description: The first post-war Czechoslovak government announces its programme in liberated Košice, recognising Slovaks as a separate nation.

title: Czechoslovakia becomes a federation
description: A constitutional law signed at Bratislava Castle creates a Slovak Socialist Republic within a federal Czechoslovakia from 1 January 1969.

title: Candle demonstration
description: Police break up a peaceful gathering of Catholics asking for religious freedom, the first mass protest against the communist government in Slovakia since 1969.

title: Constitution adopted
description: The Slovak National Council adopts the constitution of the Slovak Republic, four months before the country becomes independent.

title: Slovakia joins the European Union
description: Slovakia becomes a member of the European Union, a month after joining NATO.

title: Slovakia adopts the euro
description: The euro replaces the Slovak koruna, making Slovakia the first of the former Warsaw Pact states to join the eurozone.

title: Murder of Ján Kuciak
description: An investigative journalist and his fiancée are shot dead at home, and the protests that follow force Prime Minister Robert Fico to resign.
